::: {#fig-pmf-cdf-quantile}

```{r}
#| label: pmf-cdf-quantile-alt
#| include: false
# The alt text, saved once
# for the chunk option below
# and for the aria-label of the interactive version.
fig_alt <- paste(
  "Two rows of three plots.",
  "Top row, for the number of heads in two fair coin flips:",
  "bars of height one quarter, one half and one quarter at 0, 1 and 2;",
  "a staircase CDF rising from 0 to 1 in three jumps;",
  "and a staircase quantile function taking the values 0, 1 and 2.",
  "Bottom row, for the standard normal distribution:",
  "a bell-shaped density with the area to the left of one shaded;",
  "a smooth S-shaped CDF rising from 0 to 1;",
  "and a smooth increasing quantile function",
  "that drops toward negative infinity near probability 0",
  "and rises toward positive infinity near probability 1."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: pmf-cdf-quantile-plot
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
# HTML formats get six interactive plotly panels;
# the handout and other formats get the same panels drawn with ggplot2.
# Top row: X = number of heads in two fair coin flips,
# so the pmf is 1/4, 1/2, 1/4 on 0, 1, 2, as in the examples above.
# Bottom row: the standard normal distribution;
# the density is shaded up to t = 1
# to show that the CDF at t is the area to its left.
heads <- 0:2
pmf <- c(1, 2, 1) / 4
cdf_steps <- cumsum(pmf)
shade_at <- 1
z <- seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 300)
p_grid <- seq(0.005, 0.995, length.out = 300)
z_shade <- z[z <= shade_at]
blue <- "#1f77b4"
step_x <- c(-1, heads, 3)

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  library(plotly)

  # One panel's layout:
  # words on the axes, no plotly toolbar clutter.
  panel_layout <- function(widget, title, xlab, ylab, ...) {
    widget |>
      layout(
        title = list(
          text = title,
          font = list(size = 13)
        ),
        xaxis = list(
          title = xlab,
          zeroline = FALSE
        ),
        yaxis = list(
          title = ylab,
          zeroline = FALSE,
          ...
        ),
        showlegend = FALSE,
        margin = list(t = 40)
      ) |>
      config(
        displaylogo = FALSE,
        responsive = TRUE
      )
  }

  coin_pmf <- plot_ly(
    x = heads,
    y = pmf,
    type = "bar",
    marker = list(color = blue),
    hovertemplate = "heads %{x}<br>probability %{y}<extra></extra>"
  ) |>
    panel_layout(
      "Coin flips: mass function",
      "number of heads",
      "probability",
      range = c(0, 0.6)
    )
  coin_cdf <- plot_ly(
    x = step_x,
    y = c(0, cdf_steps, 1),
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines",
    line = list(
      shape = "hv",
      color = blue
    ),
    hovertemplate = "t %{x}<br>CDF %{y}<extra></extra>"
  ) |>
    panel_layout(
      "Coin flips: CDF",
      "t",
      "probability of at most t heads"
    )
  coin_quantile <- plot_ly(
    x = c(0, 0.25, 0.75, 1),
    y = c(0, 1, 2, 2),
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines",
    line = list(
      shape = "hv",
      color = blue
    ),
    hovertemplate = "p %{x}<br>quantile %{y}<extra></extra>"
  ) |>
    panel_layout(
      "Coin flips: quantile function",
      "probability p",
      "smallest t with CDF at least p"
    )

  normal_pdf <- plot_ly() |>
    add_lines(
      x = z,
      y = dnorm(z),
      line = list(color = blue),
      hovertemplate = "x %{x:.2f}<br>density %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>"
    ) |>
    add_trace(
      x = c(z_shade, shade_at),
      y = c(dnorm(z_shade), 0),
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines",
      fill = "tozeroy",
      fillcolor = "rgba(31,119,180,0.3)",
      line = list(width = 0),
      hoverinfo = "skip"
    ) |>
    panel_layout(
      "Normal: density",
      "x",
      "density"
    )
  normal_cdf <- plot_ly() |>
    add_lines(
      x = z,
      y = pnorm(z),
      line = list(color = blue),
      hovertemplate = "t %{x:.2f}<br>CDF %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>"
    ) |>
    add_markers(
      x = shade_at,
      y = pnorm(shade_at),
      marker = list(color = blue),
      hoverinfo = "skip"
    ) |>
    panel_layout(
      "Normal: CDF",
      "t",
      "probability of at most t"
    )
  normal_quantile <- plot_ly() |>
    add_lines(
      x = p_grid,
      y = qnorm(p_grid),
      line = list(color = blue),
      hovertemplate = "p %{x:.3f}<br>quantile %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>"
    ) |>
    panel_layout(
      "Normal: quantile function",
      "probability p",
      "quantile"
    )

  # A flex container lays the panels out in two rows of three,
  # wrapping on narrow screens.
  cell <- function(w) {
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex: 1 1 280px; min-width: 0;",
      w
    )
  }
  # The alt text: a plotly widget has none of its own.
  htmltools::div(
    role = "img",
    `aria-label` = fig_alt,
    style = "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px;",
    cell(coin_pmf),
    cell(coin_cdf),
    cell(coin_quantile),
    cell(normal_pdf),
    cell(normal_cdf),
    cell(normal_quantile)
  )
} else {
  library(ggplot2)

  panel_names <- c(
    "Coin flips: mass function",
    "Coin flips: CDF",
    "Coin flips: quantile function",
    "Normal: density",
    "Normal: CDF",
    "Normal: quantile function"
  )
  panel_data <- function(panel, x, y) {
    data.frame(
      panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_names),
      x = x,
      y = y
    )
  }

  bars <- panel_data(panel_names[1], heads, pmf)
  steps <- rbind(
    panel_data(panel_names[2], step_x, c(0, cdf_steps, 1)),
    panel_data(panel_names[3], c(0, 0.25, 0.75, 1), c(0, 1, 2, 2))
  )
  curves <- rbind(
    panel_data(panel_names[4], z, dnorm(z)),
    panel_data(panel_names[5], z, pnorm(z)),
    panel_data(panel_names[6], p_grid, qnorm(p_grid))
  )
  shaded <- panel_data(
    panel_names[4],
    c(z_shade, shade_at),
    c(dnorm(z_shade), 0)
  )
  marked <- panel_data(panel_names[5], shade_at, pnorm(shade_at))

  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_col(
      data = bars,
      fill = blue,
      width = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_step(
      data = steps,
      colour = blue
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = curves,
      colour = blue
    ) +
    geom_ribbon(
      data = shaded,
      mapping = aes(ymin = 0, ymax = y),
      fill = blue,
      alpha = 0.3
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = marked,
      colour = blue
    ) +
    facet_wrap(
      ~panel,
      nrow = 2,
      scales = "free"
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

A probability mass function, cumulative distribution function and quantile function
for a discrete random variable
(top row: the number of heads in two fair coin flips)
and a continuous one
(bottom row: the standard normal distribution).
The shaded area under the normal density up to a point equals the CDF at that point.
The quantile function reverses the CDF:
its axes are the CDF's, swapped.
:::
